stem: A transplant recipient asks about planning a vacation three months after discharge. Which travel counseling point aligns with standard post-transplant references?

options.text: Patients are typically instructed to avoid traveling away from home during the first few months post-transplant
Long-distance travel is encouraged before the first outpatient follow-up visit
Travel timing is unrestricted immediately after hospital discharge
Immunosuppression may be stopped during travel to reduce infection risk

explanation.rationale_correct: Travel teaching instructs patients to avoid traveling away from home during the first few months post-transplant, with destination planning based on current health and infection risk.

rationale_incorrect.B: Early travel away from home is discouraged during the first few months rather than encouraged before stable follow-up.
rationale_incorrect.C: Travel is restricted during early recovery rather than being unrestricted at discharge.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression must continue as prescribed; travel does not justify stopping therapy.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → o. Travel → i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: avoid traveling away from home during the first few months posttransplant

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → o. Travel → i. (avoid travel away from home first few months post-transplant); PDF p. 122 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Early post-transplant travel-away-from-home angle distinct from extensive-travel-at-discharge teaching (cctc-1023, p. 111); anchor verified on Cupples p. 122.

stem: When teaching medication planning for post-transplant travel, which instruction aligns with standard references?

options.text: Pack a 2- to 3-day supply of medications in carry-on luggage
Place all immunosuppression only in checked baggage with no carry-on supply
Travel requires discontinuing immunosuppression for the duration of the trip
Medications should be transferred to unlabeled containers before flying

explanation.rationale_correct: Travel medication teaching includes packing a 2- to 3-day supply in carry-on luggage and bringing more medication than needed in original containers in case of unexpected delays.

rationale_incorrect.B: A carry-on supply is specifically recommended rather than relying only on checked baggage.
rationale_incorrect.C: Immunosuppression must continue during travel as prescribed.
rationale_incorrect.D: Medications should be stored in original containers rather than unlabeled containers.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → o. Travel → iv. Medications
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Pack 2- to 3-day supply in carry-on luggage

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → o. Travel → iv. Medications (2–3-day carry-on supply; extra meds in original containers); PDF p. 122 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Travel medication-carry-on angle distinct from timed IS dosing (cctc-3019) and discharge medication combo (cctc-1033); anchor verified on Cupples p. 122.

stem: A kidney recipient planning international travel asks how to prepare for medical care at the destination. Which coordination step aligns with standard travel references?

options.text: Assist the patient in locating a health care provider at the destination should medical care be required
Destination medical planning is unnecessary because transplant teams manage care worldwide remotely
Recipients should travel without medication summaries to reduce luggage weight
Only emergency departments at home institutions may treat transplant travelers

explanation.rationale_correct: Travel planning includes assisting the patient in locating a health care provider at the destination if medical care is required, along with carrying a health history summary and adequate medications.

rationale_incorrect.B: Destination medical planning is recommended rather than assuming remote management alone is sufficient.
rationale_incorrect.C: Travel teaching includes bringing a summary of health history and current medications.
rationale_incorrect.D: Recipients may need local care at the destination rather than limiting treatment to the home institution only.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → o. Travel → iii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Assist patient in locating health care provider at destination should medical care be required

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → o. Travel → iii. (locate health care provider at destination); PDF p. 122 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Destination-provider planning angle distinct from early travel restriction (cctc-1134) and carry-on medication teaching (cctc-1135); anchor verified on Cupples p. 122.

stem: A coordinator is updating post-transplant travel teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Patients are typically instructed to avoid traveling away from home during the first few months post-transplant.
A 2- to 3-day medication supply should be packed in carry-on luggage.
All immunosuppression should be placed only in checked baggage with no carry-on supply.
Depending on destination, consultation with a Travel Clinic may be needed to identify health hazards and preventive medications or vaccinations.

explanation.rationale_correct: Early travel restriction, carry-on medication supply, and Travel Clinic consultation when indicated are supported. Statement III is false because a carry-on medication supply is specifically recommended.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—Travel Clinic consultation may be needed depending on destination.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because carry-on medication supply is recommended.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: avoid traveling away from home … Pack 2- to 3-day supply in carry-on luggage … consultation with Travel Clinic

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → o. Travel → i., iv., vii. (early travel restriction, carry-on meds, Travel Clinic consultation); PDF p. 122 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Travel-prep combo distinct from return-to-work combo (cctc-1133) and early-discharge travel restriction (cctc-1023); anchor verified on Cupples p. 122.
